text:
Noah: opened a tiny PR to add localized examples for structured outputs + a short note about parse fallbacks. Wanted to get quick docs review before I add more locales.
Priya: link?
Noah: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5120
Jin: skimmed . Suggest we show both the canonical JSON schema and a localized user-facing example. E.g. schema stays the same but example strings can be in es-ES and zh-CN.
Carlos: Agree. Also call out that validators (ajv) should validate shape only, not string content ; otherwise translators will fail CI because translations change text.
Priya: Good catch. We should add frontmatter flag `example: translated` to skip content checks but still run structural validation. Example frontmatter:
```yaml
---
example: translated
locale: es-ES
---
```
Noah: I'll add `example: translated` and add a CI note to only run `ajv` against `--schema` (no `pattern` checks).
Jin: Also propose a tiny Go SDK snippet showing safe parsing + fallback, since we have more Go customers:```go
resp, _ := client.CallTool(ctx, "extract_people", input)
var out []Person
if err := parseJSON(resp.Text, &out); err != nil || len(out) == 0 {
    // fallback: log + return helpful prompt to user
}
```
Carlos: Nice. For the docs text, add a short sentence: "Prefer schema-level constraints (required, minItems) and keep string patterns optional for translated examples."
docs-bot: deploy preview queued https://deploy-preview-5120--docs.redwood.example :hourglass:
Priya: one more nit : use `response.parse_json()` in Python examples to match SDK naming.
Noah: will update Python + Go snippets, add the frontmatter flag docs, and clarify CI filter. Pushing changes now, will request reviews after CI finishes. Thanks! :rocket:
